description: Roots that dreamed of being a bear. It sleeps for whole seasons, and wakes furious at whatever an axe is.
lore: Nobody ever felled this one, because it was never a tree. It is built out of the other half of an extremely ordinary memory: everyone who ever swung an axe remembers the tree going over. The crack, the hinge, the long lean, the ground coming up. Hundreds of thousands of people holding that same half-minute — and the part they kept was never their own arms. It was the tree. Enough of that pooled under one canopy and it gets up, wearing a crown of moss and mushrooms it never grew, having gone over its whole life and never once held a handle.

It sleeps whole seasons, deep enough that people who work a wood will tell you exactly where it lies and walk over it without lowering their voices. You may carry anything you like across that ground. [[characters/54bead23|Osric]] carried a new axe, hafted that morning, because he is not long woken and still counts in living years, and where he came from an axe on your shoulder meant work and nothing else. He does not remember the afternoon. He came back together at the fire that evening, short one afternoon and one good haft.

He still makes them; people need firewood, and a smith with opinions about axes is no use to anyone. But he asks now, out loud, before taking the work: what is this one for. And he goes around the north wood rather than through, which costs him an hour he does not mention. The wood has no opinion about Osric at all. It has one about the axe.
gm_notes: Made: the pooled remembering is the FELLED side of the axe-memory, not the woodcutter's side — which is why the fury is inherited rather than experienced. Osric is the right NPC because he is the only one still thinking in living-world terms; his correction (asking what a tool is for) is the character beat. No stone bound yet, so nothing is said about leavings.
